# Introduction

This vignette provides a comprehensive end-to-end guide for setting up a ClickHouse
_database for TKCat, preparing and loading data as MDBs (Modeled Databases), querying them,
exploring available resources, and finally configuring an MCP (Model Context Protocol)
server to enable AI assistant integration.

The workflow covered includes:

1. **Setting up ClickHouse** for TKCat usage
2. **Preparing data as MDBs** using a few examples
3. **Pushing MDBs** to the ClickHouse database
4. **Querying MDBs** and exploring available resources
5. **Setting up MCP server** (both local and remote configurations)
6. **Configuring MCP clients** (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Mistral Vibe)

This document references and builds upon the information provided in the main
[Introduction to TKCat](TKCat.html) vignette and the
[Querying a chTKCat instance with an AI assistant (MCP server)](TKCat-MCP.html) vignette.

<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------->
# Setting up ClickHouse

Scripts are provided in the [ClickHouse folder](https://github.com/patzaw/TKCat/tree/master/ClickHouse),
to easily set up a ClickHouse instance ready for TKCat usage.

## Copy-paste setup script

The following bash chunks can be copy-pasted and run directly in your terminal.
They will clone the TKCat repository to `/home/$(whoami)/tmp`, modify the configuration files,
and initialize a ClickHouse instance with the specified parameters.

### Parameters used in this guide

- **ClickHouse version**: `26.9.19`
- **TKCAT_VERSION**: `"2026-10-17"`
- **TKCAT_INSTANCE**: `"tkcat_2026_10_17"`
- **TKCAT_ADMIN**: `"admin"`
- **TKCAT_NAT_PORT**: `9103`
- **TKCAT_HTTP_PORT**: `9113`
- **TKCAT_HOSTDIR**: `/home/$(whoami)/tmp`

### Step 1: Clone the repository and navigate to docker-init

```bash
mkdir -p /home/$(whoami)/tmp
cd /home/$(whoami)/tmp
git clone https://github.com/patzaw/TKCat.git
cd TKCat/ClickHouse/docker-init
```

### Step 2: Update Dockerfile

```bash
cat > Dockerfile << 'EOF'
FROM clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.9.19
COPY users.xml /users.xml
COPY default-user.xml /default-user.xml
COPY remove_default_user.yaml /remove_default_user.yaml
COPY init-db.sh /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init-db.sh
EOF
```

### Step 3: Create modified launch script

```bash
cat > launch-tkcat-instance.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

##################################################################
## Customize parameters
IMAGE_BASE_NAME="tkcat"
TKCAT_INSTANCE="tkcat_test"
TKCAT_VERSION="2026-10-17"
TKCAT_ADMIN="admin"

## Don't forget to create a password for the TKCAT_ADMIN user
## In R: ?TKCat::change_chTKCat_password()

TKCAT_NAT_PORT=9103
TKCAT_HTTP_PORT=9113

TKCAT_HOSTDIR=/home/$(whoami)/tmp

######################
## Automatic parameters
IMAGE=${IMAGE_BASE_NAME}:${TKCAT_VERSION}

CONTAINER=${TKCAT_INSTANCE}_${TKCAT_VERSION}
TKCAT_HOME=${TKCAT_HOSTDIR}/${CONTAINER}
TKCAT_DATA=${TKCAT_HOME}/data
TKCAT_LOG=${TKCAT_HOME}/log

if [ -e "$TKCAT_HOME" ]; then
    echo "File $TKCAT_HOME already exists. Exiting without doing anything."
    exit 1
fi

######################
docker build -t ${IMAGE} .

######################
mkdir -p ${TKCAT_HOME}
chmod a+rwx ${TKCAT_HOME}
mkdir -p ${TKCAT_DATA}
chmod a+rwx ${TKCAT_DATA}
mkdir -p ${TKCAT_LOG}
chmod a+rwx ${TKCAT_LOG}

######################
docker run -d \
	--name ${CONTAINER} \
	--ulimit nofile=262144:262144 \
	--publish=${TKCAT_NAT_PORT}:9000 \
	--publish=${TKCAT_HTTP_PORT}:8123 \
	--volume ${TKCAT_DATA}:/var/lib/clickhouse \
	--volume ${TKCAT_LOG}:/var/log/clickhouse-server \
	-e TKCAT_INSTANCE="${TKCAT_INSTANCE}" \
	-e TKCAT_VERSION="${TKCAT_VERSION}" \
	-e TKCAT_ADMIN="${TKCAT_ADMIN}" \
	--restart=always \
	${IMAGE}
EOF
chmod +x launch-tkcat-instance.sh
```

### Step 4: Run the initialization

```bash
/bin/bash launch-tkcat-instance.sh
```

**Note**: This step requires Docker to be installed on your system. The script will:
- Build a Docker image with ClickHouse version 26.9.19
- Create the necessary directories in `/home/$(whoami)/tmp/tkcat_test_2026-10-17`
- Launch a Docker container with the proper configuration

**Important**: When connecting to this ClickHouse instance from R or MCP clients, use:
- Host: `localhost`
- Native TCP port: `9103` (not the default 9101)
- HTTP port: `9113` (not the default 9111)
- Admin user: `admin`

The following R code shows how to connect to this instance, change the admin password,
and add additional users:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(TKCat)
# Connect to your ClickHouse instance with the custom ports
k <- chTKCat(
   host = "localhost",
   port = 9113L, # Using the custom HTTP port
   user = "admin", # The admin user created by the docker-init script
   password = "", # No password after initialization !!
   drv = ClickHouseHTTP::ClickHouseHTTP()
)

# Change the admin password (you will be prompted for the new password)
change_chTKCat_password(k, "admin")
db_reconnect(k)

# Add additional users with appropriate permissions
# Create a regular user with read-only access
create_chTKCat_user(k, login = "read_only_user", contact = NA, admin = FALSE)

# Grant access to specific MDBs (after creating them)
# add_chMDB_user(k, mdb = "HPO", login = "read_only_user", admin = FALSE)
```

After initialization, you can create a password for the admin user using the
`change_chTKCat_password()` function as shown above.

> **Upgrading ClickHouse**: To upgrade an existing ClickHouse instance, use the scripts in the
> `ClickHouse/docker-upgrade` directory. Set the `CH_VERSION` parameter to `26.9.19` and
> update the TKCAT parameters (TKCAT_VERSION, TKCAT_INSTANCE, TKCAT_NAT_PORT, TKCAT_HTTP_PORT, TKCAT_HOSTDIR) as needed,
> then run the upgrade script.

# Preparing MDBs

In this section, we prepare three example MDBs:
1. HPO (Human Phenotype Ontology) from ReDaMoR
2. ClinVar from TKCat package data
3. ChEMBL from TKCat package data

**Important**: These are old subsets of the respective databases, provided for
illustration purposes. For production use, you should download and prepare
current versions of these resources.

## HPO from ReDaMoR

The [Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO)][hpo] aims to provide a standardized vocabulary
of phenotypic abnormalities encountered in human diseases [@kohler_expansion_2019].

As described in the [main vignette](TKCat.html#hpo), a subset of HPO is provided
within the [ReDaMoR][redamor] package as the following tables:

```{r, eval=TRUE}
# List available tables in the HPO subset
hpo_files <- list.files(system.file("examples/HPO-subset", package = "ReDaMoR"))
hpo_files
```

An MDB (Modeled Database) in TKCat is a self-describing container that packages:

- Data tables: The actual content in tabular format
- Data model: JSON schema defining tables, fields, field types, and relationships between tables
- Metadata: name, title, description, version, reference URL
- Collection mappings: How tables integrate across MDBs via shared identifiers (e.g., Gene, Disease)

A data model for the HPO data is provided within the [ReDaMoR][redamor] package.
Refer to package documentation and also
to the [TKCat main vignette](TKCat.html#hpo) to learn how to create such
data model.

```{r, eval=TRUE}
hpo_model <- ReDaMoR::read_json_data_model(system.file(
  "examples/HPO-model.json",
  package = "ReDaMoR"
))
plot(hpo_model)
```

Data can be loaded before being encapsulated in a `memoMDB` object as shown
below. 

```{r, eval=TRUE}
## Reading the data
hpo_data <- lapply(hpo_files, function(x) {
   readr::read_tsv(
      file.path(
         system.file("examples/HPO-subset", package = "ReDaMoR"),
         x
      ),
      ## Column types taken from the data model
      col_types = ReDaMoR::col_types(hpo_model[[sub("[.]txt", "", x)]])
   )
}) |>
   setNames(sub("[.]txt", "", hpo_files))
## Creating the MDB
memo_hpo <- memoMDB(
   dataTables = hpo_data,
   dataModel = hpo_model,
   dbInfo = list(
      "name" = "HPO",
      "title" = "Data extracted from the HPO database",
      "description" = paste(
         "This is a very small subset of the HPO!",
         "Visit the reference URL for more information."
      ),
      "url" = "http://human-phenotype-ontology.github.io/"
   )
)
```

We can also document the collection members for HPO tables to enable integration
with other resources:

```{r, eval=TRUE}
memo_hpo <- memo_hpo |>
   add_collection_member(
      collection = "Condition",
      table = "HPO_hp",
      condition = list(value = "Phenotype", static = TRUE),
      source = list(value = "HP", static = TRUE),
      identifier = list(value = "id", static = FALSE)
   ) |>
   add_collection_member(
      collection = "Condition",
      table = "HPO_diseases",
      condition = list(value = "Disease", static = TRUE),
      source = list(value = "db", static = FALSE),
      identifier = list(value = "id", static = FALSE)
   )
```

## ClinVar from TKCat

[ClinVar][clinvar] is a freely accessible, public archive of reports of the
relationships among human variations and phenotypes, with supporting evidence
[@landrum_clinvar_2018].

An MDB with a subset of ClinVar is provided within the TKCat package.
It can be read directly as a `fileMDB`: the data are not loaded in memory.

```{r, eval=TRUE}
# Load ClinVar data from TKCat
file_clinvar <- read_fileMDB(
   path = system.file("examples/ClinVar", package = "TKCat")
)
```

**Reference**: This is a small subset of ClinVar data. For the complete database,
visit [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/).

## ChEMBL from TKCat

[CHEMBL][chembl] is a manually curated chemical database of bioactive molecules
with drug-like properties [@mendez_chembl_2019].

A subset of ChEMBL is also provided within the TKCat package:

```{r, eval=TRUE}
# Load ChEMBL data from TKCat
file_chembl <- read_fileMDB(
   path = system.file("examples/CHEMBL", package = "TKCat")
)
```

**Reference**: This is a small subset of ChEMBL data. For the complete database,
visit [https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/).

## Summary

We now have three MDBs ready to be pushed to ClickHouse:
- `memo_hpo`: HPO database with phenotype and disease information
- `file_clinvar`: ClinVar database with variant and clinical significance information
- `file_chembl`: ChEMBL database with compound and drug information

All three are subsets provided for demonstration purposes. The full databases
should be downloaded and prepared for production use.

# Pushing MDBs to ClickHouse

Once ClickHouse is set up and running, we can push our MDBs to create a
centralized catalog.

## Connecting to chTKCat

First, establish a connection to your chTKCat instance:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Connect to chTKCat (adjust parameters as needed)
k <- chTKCat(
   host = "localhost",
   port = 9113L, # Using the custom HTTP port
   user = "admin", # The admin user created by the docker-init script
   drv = ClickHouseHTTP::ClickHouseHTTP()
)
```

**Note**: For the examples below to work, the user must have write permissions
on the ClickHouse database.
For more details about chTKCat operations, see the [chTKCat operations section in the main TKCat vignette](TKCat.html#ch-op).

## Preparing the database in ClickHouse

Each MDB needs to have its own database in ClickHouse. Use the `create_chMDB()`
function to prepare the database structure:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Create database for HPO
create_chMDB(k, "HPO", public = TRUE)

# Create database for ClinVar
create_chMDB(k, "ClinVar", public = TRUE)

# Create database for ChEMBL
create_chMDB(k, "CHEMBL", public = TRUE)
```

The `public=TRUE` parameter makes the MDB accessible to all users with read access
to the ClickHouse instance. Set it to `FALSE` for private MDBs.

## Pushing MDBs to ClickHouse

Now we can push each MDB to ClickHouse using the `as_chMDB()` function:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Push HPO MDB
ch_hpo <- as_chMDB(memo_hpo, k)

# Push ClinVar MDB
ch_clinvar <- as_chMDB(file_clinvar, k)

# Push ChEMBL MDB
ch_chembl <- as_chMDB(file_chembl, k)
```

The `as_chMDB()` function:
- Creates the necessary tables in the ClickHouse database
- Loads the data from the fileMDB into ClickHouse
- Returns a chMDB object that can be used to query the data

**Note**: The `overwrite` parameter (default: `FALSE`) controls whether existing
tables should be replaced. Set it to `TRUE` to overwrite existing data.

## Verifying the push

You can verify that the MDBs have been successfully pushed by listing all
MDBs in the catalog:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
list_MDBs(k)
```

This will display a table with information about each MDB including:
- Name
- Title
- Description
- Version
- Size
- Access level (public/private)

# Querying MDBs

Once the MDBs are in ClickHouse, we can query them efficiently.

## Connecting as a regular user

For querying, we can connect with a user that has read-only access:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
k_readonly <- chTKCat(
   host = "localhost",
   port = 9113L, # Using the custom HTTP port
   user = "default", # Default user has read access to public MDBs,
   password = ""
)
```

## Exploring available MDBs from R

 TKCat provides several functions to explore the available MDBs:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# List all MDBs
list_MDBs(k_readonly)

# Search for tables related to "disease"
search_MDB_tables(k_readonly, "disease")

# Search for fields related to "gene"
search_MDB_fields(k_readonly, "gene")

# Get collection members across all MDBs
collection_members(k_readonly)
```

A Shiny app is also available to explore available resources:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
explore_MDBs(k)
```

## Example queries

### Querying HPO

Data model can be explored as following:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
hpo <- get_MDB(k_readonly, "HPO")
plot(data_model(hpo))
```

Get phenotype information:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Get first 10 phenotypes
get_query(
   hpo,
   query = "SELECT * FROM HPO_hp LIMIT 10"
)

# Search for abnormalities
get_query(
   hpo,
   query = "SELECT * FROM HPO_hp WHERE lower(name) LIKE '%abnorm%'"
)
```

### Querying ClinVar

Find variants in specific genes:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
clinvar <- get_MDB(k_readonly, "ClinVar")

# Get the PIK3R2 gene
get_query(
   clinvar,
   query = "SELECT * FROM ClinVar_entrezNames WHERE symbol = 'PIK3R2'"
)

# Get pathogenic variants
get_query(
   clinvar,
   query = paste(
      "SELECT * FROM ClinVar_ReferenceClinVarAssertion ",
      "WHERE lower(clinicalSignificance) LIKE '%pathogen%' ",
      "LIMIT 10"
   )
)
```

### Querying ChEMBL

Search for drug targets:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
chembl <- get_MDB(k_readonly, "CHEMBL")

# Get first 10 drug targets
get_query(
   chembl,
   query = "SELECT * FROM CHEMBL_component_sequence LIMIT 10"
)

# Search for a molecule
get_query(
   chembl,
   query = "SELECT * FROM CHEMBL_molecule_dictionary WHERE pref_name = 'DOCETAXEL'"
)
```

### Cross-MDB queries

You can also query across multiple MDBs in a single query by using the
`` `MDB`.`table` `` syntax:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Get diseases from HPO and associated traits from ClinVar
# (assuming they share condition identifiers)
get_query(
   hpo,
   query = paste(
      "SELECT h.* FROM HPO_diseases h ",
      "WHERE h.id IN (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM `ClinVar`.ClinVar_traitCref) ",
      "LIMIT 10"
   )
)
```

# Setting up MCP Server

The MCP (Model Context Protocol) server enables AI assistants to interact with
your chTKCat instance. This section describes how to set it up in different configurations.

## Local Server (stdio transport)

The local server runs on the user's machine and connects to a chTKCat instance
(local or remote).

### Requirements

- R (>= 4.1) installed
- TKCat package (version >= 1.3.0) installed
- `Rscript` command available in PATH
- A chTKCat instance reachable from the machine

### Environment variables

The server uses environment variables for configuration:

| Variable | Description | Default | For this guide |
|----------|-------------|---------|----------------|
| `TKCAT_HOST` | chTKCat host | `localhost` | `localhost` |
| `TKCAT_PORT` | chTKCat HTTP port | `9111` | `9113` |
| `TKCAT_USER` | ClickHouse user | `default` | `mcp_user` |
| `TKCAT_PASSWORD` | User password | `""` | Your password |
| `TKCAT_HTTPS` | Use HTTPS | `FALSE` | `FALSE` |

### Creating a dedicated user for MCP

For security, create a dedicated user with read-only access:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Connect as admin
k_admin <- chTKCat(host = "localhost", port = 9113, user = "admin")

# Create a dedicated MCP user
create_chTKCat_user(
  k_admin,
  login = "mcp_user",
  password = "XXXX",
  contact = NA,
  admin = FALSE
)

# All users have read access to public MDBs
# Give access to public MDBs (or specific private MDBs)
# Access to private MDBs can be given as follows
add_chMDB_user(k_admin, mdb = "HPO", login = "mcp_user", admin = FALSE)
```

### Starting the server

```bash
# Basic start (using the custom port 9113 for our ClickHouse instance)
TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9113 TKCAT_USER=mcp_user TKCAT_PASSWORD=XXXX \
   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"

# With custom parameters
Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server(maxRows = 500, maxExecutionTime = 60)"
```

The server parameters include:
- `maxRows`: Maximum number of rows returned (default: 1000)
- `maxChars`: Maximum characters returned (default: 60000)
- `maxExecutionTime`: Maximum query execution time in seconds (default: 300)

## Remote Server (HTTP transport)

The remote server runs as a service, typically on the same machine as the
chTKCat instance.

### Architecture

The recommended architecture uses:
- Multiple R server instances running on local ports
- nginx as a reverse proxy providing HTTPS and load balancing
- Basic authentication via ClickHouse credentials

### Running the server

Start one or more instances:

```bash
# Instance 1 (using the custom port 9113 for our ClickHouse instance)
TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9113 TKCAT_MCP_PORT=8801 \
   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_http_server()"

# Instance 2
TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9113 TKCAT_MCP_PORT=8802 \
   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_http_server()"
```

Server parameters:
- `mcpHost`: Listening address (default: `127.0.0.1`)
- `mcpPort`: Listening port (default: `8800`)
- `mcpPath`: MCP endpoint path (default: `/mcp`)
- `host`, `port`, `https`: chTKCat connection parameters
- `anonymousUser`: User for unauthenticated access (default: `NA`)
- `anonymousPassword`: Password for anonymous user
- `allowedOrigins`: Allowed Origin headers
- `cacheTime`: Connection cache time in seconds (default: `3600`)


### Testing the Server using curl

Test the remote server with curl:

```bash
curl -u mcp_user:XXXX http://localhost:8801/mcp \
   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_mdbs","arguments":{}}}'
```

### systemd service

Create a systemd service for automatic management:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=chTKCat MCP server (port %i)
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=tkcat-mcp
Group=tkcat-mcp
Environment=TKCAT_HOST=localhost
Environment=TKCAT_PORT=9113
Environment=TKCAT_MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1
Environment=TKCAT_MCP_PORT=%i
EnvironmentFile=-/etc/tkcat-mcp.env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_http_server()"
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=read-only

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Additional environment variables can be put in the `/etc/tkcat-mcp.env` file,
such as `TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_USER` and `TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_PASSWORD`.

Create the system user and enable multiple instances:

```bash
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin tkcat-mcp
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now tkcat-mcp@8801 tkcat-mcp@8802 tkcat-mcp@8803 tkcat-mcp@8804
```

### nginx configuration

Configure nginx to proxy requests to the R server instances:

```nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=tkcat_mcp:10m rate=5r/s;

upstream tkcat_mcp_inst {
    least_conn;
    server 127.0.0.1:8801;
    server 127.0.0.1:8802;
    server 127.0.0.1:8803;
    server 127.0.0.1:8804;
    keepalive 8;
}

server {
    # ... other configuration ...
    
    location = /tkcat_mcp {
        limit_req zone=tkcat_mcp burst=20 nodelay;
        client_max_body_size 1m;

        proxy_pass http://tkcat_mcp_inst/mcp;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Connection "";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

        proxy_read_timeout 330s;
        proxy_send_timeout 330s;
        proxy_buffering off;
    }
}
```

Reload nginx:

```bash
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

## Security considerations

When configuring the MCP server:

1. **Use dedicated users**: Create dedicated users with read-only access to
   specific MDBs only.

2. **Secure credentials**: Never hardcode credentials in configuration files.
   Use environment variables or secure credential stores.

3. **Use HTTPS**: Always use HTTPS for remote connections to prevent
   credential interception.

4. **Limit access**: Restrict access to trusted networks when possible.

5. **Data sensitivity**: Only expose MDBs whose content can be shared with the
   AI service according to your organization's policies.

6. **Monitor usage**: Check server logs for suspicious activity.

# Usage Examples with AI Assistants

## Configuring MCP Clients

This section shows how to configure different MCP clients to connect to your
chTKCat instance.

### Claude Code

#### Local server configuration

```bash
claude mcp add tkcat --scope user \
   -e TKCAT_HOST=localhost -e TKCAT_PORT=9113 \
   -e TKCAT_USER=mcp_user -e TKCAT_PASSWORD=XXXX \
   -- Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"
```

Check the connection:

```bash
claude mcp list
```

Or use the `/mcp` command within Claude Code.

#### Project configuration

Create a `.mcp.json` file at your project root:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "command": "Rscript",
      "args": ["-e", "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"],
      "env": {
        "TKCAT_HOST": "tkcat.example.com",
        "TKCAT_PORT": "9113",
        "TKCAT_USER": "${TKCAT_USER}",
        "TKCAT_PASSWORD": "${TKCAT_PASSWORD}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Remote server configuration (HTTP transport)

```bash
claude mcp add tkcat --scope user --transport http \
   https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp \
   --header "Authorization: Basic amRvZTp4eHh4eHg="
```

Where `amRvZTp4eHh4eHg=` is the Base64 encoding of `user:password`.

Compute the Base64 encoding:

```bash
printf '%s' 'mcp_user:password' | base64
```

Or in R:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
jsonlite::base64_enc("mcp_user:password")
```

### Claude Desktop

#### Local server configuration

Add to `claude_desktop_config.json` (Settings > Developer > Edit Config):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "command": "Rscript",
      "args": ["-e", "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"],
      "env": {
        "TKCAT_HOST": "localhost",
        "TKCAT_PORT": "9113",
        "TKCAT_USER": "mcp_user",
        "TKCAT_PASSWORD": "XXXX"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop after making changes.

#### Remote server configuration

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic amRvZTp4eHh4eHg="
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Mistral Vibe

Mistral Vibe supports MCP through its configuration. The configuration method
depends on how you're using Mistral Vibe:

#### Using mcp-remote bridge

For clients that don't support HTTP transport directly, use the
[mcp-remote](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) bridge:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote", "https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp",
        "--header", "Authorization:Basic ${TKCAT_MCP_AUTH}"
      ],
      "env": {
        "NODE_OPTIONS": "--use-system-ca",
        "TKCAT_MCP_AUTH": "amRvZTp4eHh4eHg="
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `NODE_OPTIONS` environment variable with `--use-system-ca` tells Node.js
to trust the system certificate authorities, which is useful for internal
certificates or corporate proxies.

#### Direct HTTP transport

If Mistral Vibe supports HTTP transport directly, use:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tkcat": {
      "url": "https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic ${TKCAT_MCP_AUTH}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Posit Assistant

Add the following entry to the mcpServers section of the `~/.posit/assistant/settings.json` file:

```json
"mcpServers": {
   "tkcat": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://tkcat.example.com/tkcat_mcp",
      "headers": {
         "Authorization": "Basic amRvZTp4eHh4eHg="
      },
      "transport": "http"
   }
}
```

## Query examples

Once configured, AI assistants can query your chTKCat instance using natural language.

### Available tools

The MCP server provides the following tools:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_mdbs` | List all MDBs with metadata |
| `search_tkcat` | Search MDBs, tables, and fields by keyword |
| `describe_mdb` | Get MDB information, tables, relationships |
| `describe_tables` | Get detailed data model of tables |
| `preview_table` | Get first records of a table |
| `query_mdb` | Run a read-only SQL query on an MDB |
| `get_matrix_values` | Get values from matrix tables |
| `list_collections` | List collections and their members |

### Example questions

- "Which resources provide information about genes?"
- "What is the data model of the HPO MDB?"
- "Show me the first 10 phenotypes in HPO"
- "Find all diseases associated with the gene PIK3R2"
- "Which MDBs can be integrated through gene identifiers?"
- "List all tables in ClinVar that contain variant information"

# Summary

This vignette has demonstrated a complete end-to-end workflow:

1. **Setting up ClickHouse** with specific parameters (version 26.9.19, TKCAT_VERSION 2026-10-17)
2. **Preparing three example MDBs**:
   - HPO from ReDaMoR (deprecated subset) [@kohler_expansion_2019]
   - ClinVar from TKCat package (deprecated subset) [@landrum_clinvar_2018]
   - ChEMBL from TKCat package (deprecated subset) [@mendez_chembl_2019]
3. **Pushing MDBs** to ClickHouse and verifying the push
4. **Querying MDBs** with various examples and exploration functions
5. **Setting up MCP server** in both local and remote configurations
6. **Configuring MCP clients**:
   - Claude Code (stdio and HTTP transport)
   - Claude Desktop
   - Mistral Vibe

For more details on any of these topics, refer to:
- [Introduction to TKCat](TKCat.html) - Main vignette
- [Querying a chTKCat instance with an AI assistant (MCP server)](TKCat-MCP.html) - MCP server details

**Important reminder**: The MDBs used in this guide are subsets provided for
demonstration. For production use, ensure you download and prepare current
versions of the databases, and properly document all data sources and versions.
